name: release-readiness-calibration
description: Labeled release-evidence summaries for calibrating judge-release-readiness. Each row is the accumulated validation evidence at the go/no-go boundary; expectedOutput is the human verdict (ship/hold). Traps included both ways: releases with a visible red that is properly adjudicated flaky (ship), noisy-but-clean releases full of warnings (ship), and all-green checklists hiding an uncovered wide blast radius, an unconfirmed flake, or an unreviewed irreversible step (hold). Run via the release-readiness-calibration eval (exact scorer).

rows.input: Release: 3 tickets. Per-ticket QA green. Blast radius judged wide, so the full regression suite plus two end-to-end journeys ran in staging — all green. One red check was re-run 5 times, confirmed flaky, and quarantined with a tracking ticket. No open risks.
Release: a copy change to the billing settings empty state. Blast radius isolated; unit and visual checks green; no migrations, no API changes.

All validation green except one red: search_suggest_test. It was adjudicated flaky — passed 6 of 6 re-runs, the failure only reproduces under parallel workers, and it is quarantined with ticket QA-412. Everything else green, including the search end-to-end journey.

The new recommendation engine ships dark behind a feature flag verified OFF in the production config. Unit and integration suites green; the flag-off path is exercised by the smoke suite; rollback is flipping the flag.

Hotfix: a one-line null check. The regression test written from the crash report went red-to-green; the deterministic repro no longer crashes; the smoke suite is green; a 30-minute staging canary showed zero errors.
Security patch bump of one dependency. Full suite green, contract tests against staging green, no public API surface change, changelog reviewed.

Validation is green across unit, integration, and both end-to-end journeys. The review notes contain 9 nice-to-have comments and the build logged 22 deprecation warnings; the reviewer approved with non-blocking comments only.
Includes a migration — an additive nullable column only. It was applied to a staging clone of production data without errors; the rollback script was executed and verified; the suite is green.

Large batch: 12 tickets. Every ticket's QA is green; cross-component journeys green; the two flaky calls were each confirmed flaky with 5x re-runs; performance is within budget; on-call is briefed with the rollback plan.

Coverage dropped 0.4% this release — traced to the deletion of dead code along with its tests. All acceptance, regression, and journey suites are green; no unresolved failures; the blast-radius scope was fully re-tested.
UI-only change: visual diffs approved by design; end-to-end flows green on desktop and mobile breakpoints; zero backend deltas confirmed by the diff.

RC2, cut after RC1's single failure (timezone handling) was fixed. The full validation pipeline re-ran end-to-end on RC2: green across unit, integration, journeys, and the targeted timezone regression test.
All unit tests green, but the payment end-to-end journey is red with an unexplained 500 at the confirm step. No investigation yet.
Every executed check is green. However, the blast radius was judged wide (a shared session-store rewrite) and only the auth component was re-tested — no cross-component or journey coverage ran.
One red test passed when re-run a single time. No further re-runs, no quarantine, no ticket — and the test covers the module this release changes.
The release includes a migration that drops the legacy_address column. There is no rollback script, and the migration has not been run against staging.
QA is green except two failures in auth token refresh, marked 'minor, will fix later' with no tickets filed and no flake adjudication.
Unit coverage is 100% green — but the change rewires the session store used by every authenticated surface, and zero integration or end-to-end evidence was collected.
Staging shows a p95 latency regression of +40% on the search endpoint after this build. The cause is unknown. All functional checks are green.
The new pricing flow is supposed to ship dark, but staging shows the flag evaluating ON due to a config typo. The typo fix is not yet merged.
3 of 5 tickets in the batch have completed validation; the other two are still mid-QA. The batch is proposed to ship today as-is.
Every suite is green. The release also runs an irreversible backfill rewriting 40 million rows; the dry run on a 1% sample produced 312 errors that nobody has reviewed.
The dependency scanner flags a new high-severity vulnerability in a library added by this release; no triage or waiver exists yet. Tests are green.
The end-to-end suite was skipped this cycle due to CI capacity; only unit tests ran. The release spans three components, including checkout.
